overview: This Senate resolution marks one year since the July 13, 2024, attempt to assassinate President Donald J. Trump at a rally in Butler, Pennsylvania. It condemns that attack and a second attempt in West Palm Beach, Florida, on September 15, 2024. It honors Corey Comperatore, who was killed while shielding his family, and David Dutch and James Copenhaver, who were critically injured, and thanks the law enforcement officers, first responders and medical staff who responded. It also cites other recent attacks on elected officials, calls on all Americans to unite against political violence, and condemns those who incite violence against political officials. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on August 1, 2025.
for: Supporters say a unified Senate condemnation of political violence honors the victims and sends a clear message that attacks on public officials have no place in American democracy.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic: it doesn't change any law or provide new resources for protecting officials or preventing political violence.
